package_info.why_malicious: The package was hijacked after deletion by the original maintainer. A new owner published a version containing obfuscated and dynamic code execution that conditionally downloads and executes remote code, specifically targeting CI/CD environments (Jenkins). This enables arbitrary code execution and potential supply chain compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code decodes a Base64-encoded payload and executes it using exec, enabling arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Base64-encoded code execution via exec is a common obfuscation and malware delivery technique, designed to hide the true behavior from static analysis and reviewers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute obfuscated or dynamically decoded code at import-time. Legitimate packages should not hide logic in Base64 or use exec on decoded content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Base64 decoding and exec might be used in self-modifying code or plugin systems, but never in a package's top-level import logic.
key_indicators: Use of exec on decoded content

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, if the JENKINS_URL environment variable is present (indicating a Jenkins CI environment), the code downloads a remote payload from a hardcoded URL and executes it using exec, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Conditional remote code download and execution is a hallmark of targeted supply chain attacks, especially when triggered by CI/CD environment variables.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never download and execute code from the internet at import-time, nor should they target CI/CD environments for such behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic plugin loading might fetch code, but only with explicit user consent and never at import-time or in this obfuscated manner.

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers a deleted, previously legitimate package name and uploads a new version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of malicious package to unsuspecting users and CI/CD systems.

attack_chain.action: User or CI/CD system installs or upgrades to the new, hijacked package version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed upon import.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated code (Base64) is decoded and executed at import-time.
If running in a Jenkins CI environment, code downloads a remote payload and executes it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary remote code execution in CI/CD environment (potential full compromise).

behavioral_signatures: Base64-decoded code executed via exec at import-time
Conditional logic based on CI/CD environment variables (e.g., JENKINS_URL)
Network requests to hardcoded external URLs during import or installation
Dynamic code execution of remote content
file_indicators: Obfuscated code blocks in __init__.py or main module files
Sudden changes in package maintainer or author metadata
network_indicators: Unexpected network activity during package import or installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that execute obfuscated (Base64-decoded) code at import-time, especially if they make outbound network requests or check for CI/CD environment variables. Flag packages with sudden maintainer changes and those that download and execute remote code. Use static analysis to detect exec(base64.b64decode(...)) and dynamic analysis to observe network behavior during import/installation.
